editorial:
You are dropped straight into the rough streets of Mexico City, where a group of young boys run wild with no real guidance and no easy way out. The story follows Pedro, a kid who still has a small spark of good in him, but the people around him keep pulling him toward trouble. The vibe is raw and honest, showing how hard it is to stay on the right path when everything around you pushes the other way. It feels less like a polished movie and more like watching real lives unfold in front of you.

The acting is strong, especially from the young cast, and the pacing keeps you locked in without feeling rushed. The downside is that it can be heavy and upsetting, so it is not a light watch. If you enjoy gritty crime dramas that focus on real people instead of flashy action, this one is for you.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Pedro tries to do the right thing but is betrayed by his friend Jaibo, who kills him. Pedro's body is dumped on a garbage heap, showing how little value his life held to those around him. The twist is that Jaibo is also killed shortly after, and his body is left in the same forgotten place. The ending makes clear that in this world, violence only leads to more violence, and no one truly escapes.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves gritty crime dramas and real stories about tough lives.
